summary.headline: Kranti Industries crossed ₹100 crore consolidated revenue in FY26 (+28%), with standalone PAT of ₹260 lakh versus a ₹75 lakh loss in FY25.
summary.overview: FY26 was described by management as transformational: consolidated revenue crossed ₹100 crore for the first time, and the company returned to profit. Standalone revenue rose 30% to ₹93.88 crore, with EBITDA up 63.7% to ₹1244 lakh and margin improving from 10.5% to 13.3%. Q4 standalone revenue of ₹29.31 crore was the highest quarterly figure on record, up 60.2% YoY and 28.2% QoQ, though Q4 EBITDA of ₹167 lakh reflects startup costs at the new Jaipur plant. The company also entered defence machining via AVNL orders and took over a Jaipur plant on lease from 1 January 2026.

segments.name: Agriculture / tractors
segments.commentary: Management described tractors as the major revenue source; agriculture was about 95% of revenue five years ago at around ₹20 crore. Management said non-agri diversification now stands at about 16%.

segments.name: EV components
segments.commentary: EV-related components contributed about 5.3% of FY26 revenue across Kalyani Techno Forge (one passenger-car EV part, one production line running for about 12-15 months), Dana group and Eka Mobility.

segments.name: Defence
segments.commentary: Entered defence via machining orders from AVNL in FY26. Management is targeting PSU customers directly rather than as a Tier-2/3 supplier; the company expects it to take 4-6 quarters to build a substantial position.

segments.name: Jaipur plant (Plant-4)
segments.commentary: Fourth facility, adding more than 35,000 sq ft of machining capacity, with commercial operations from 1 January 2026. Utilisation was below 40% in its first quarter, and FY27 revenue guidance is ₹12-14 crore.

guidance_outlook: Management expects double-digit YoY revenue growth from here, subject to no extraordinary events.
EBITDA margin expected to stabilise at 18-20% at about 85% utilisation with a richer product mix, targeted for FY28 rather than FY27.
Plant-4 Jaipur revenue expected at ₹12-14 crore in FY27.
Priorities for FY27: ramp Jaipur utilisation, expand exports, deepen presence in defence, industrial, construction equipment and EV, and improve working capital efficiency.
No immediate acquisition planned, but inorganic growth remains part of the Vision 2030 roadmap.
capex_capacity: Jaipur facility (Plant-4) commissioned; commercial production from 1 January 2026, adding more than 35,000 sq ft of machining capacity.
Jaipur plant, machinery, instruments and business were taken on lease, with an exclusive arrangement under which the counterparty routes 100% of its machining through Kranti.
Pune facility utilisation is about 65%; management sees 80-85% as the maximum optimised level, leaving roughly 35% headroom.
Continued investment in CNC machining, automation and quality systems.
Management did not state a specific capex figure for FY27.
demand_pricing: Management cited steady domestic tractor growth over three years and recovering European and American agriculture demand as tailwinds.
Supply chain and inflation pressures from the ongoing war were noted; management said customers are supportive and solutions are being worked on.
Defence sales depend on lengthy PSU tendering processes, which management said slows order flow.
China Plus One sourcing and localisation are cited as demand drivers for the company's precision components.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the Kalyani Techno Forge relationship and EV revenue contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: One EV passenger-car component has been supplied to KTFL for 12-15 months on one production line; further volumes are under discussion. EV components were about 5.3% of FY26 revenue, covering KTFL, Dana and Eka Mobility.

qa_highlights.question: Is there distress in rural demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no; domestic tractor demand has grown for three years and European and American agriculture demand has started to recover.

qa_highlights.question: Pune utilisation and headroom?
qa_highlights.answer: Pune is at about 65% utilisation against a practical maximum of 80-85%, leaving about 35% headroom.

qa_highlights.question: Expected revenue from the Jaipur Plant-4?
qa_highlights.answer: Plant-4 utilisation was below 40% in its first quarter, and management expects ₹12-14 crore of revenue in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What does the Jaipur acquisition add?
qa_highlights.answer: It gives entry into the northern auto-ancillary belt, a ready plant with business, and a dedicated customer who will route 100% of its machining to Kranti under an exclusive agreement.

qa_highlights.question: How fast can defence scale and what is the approach?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is targeting PSU customers directly, not as a Tier-2/3 supplier, and expects 4-6 quarters to build a substantial position because of the tender process.

qa_highlights.question: Where will EBITDA margins settle?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects 18-20% EBITDA margin at about 85% utilisation, reached by FY28 rather than FY27.

risks_watch: Jaipur ramp-up: utilisation was below 40% in Q4, and Q4 EBITDA was only ₹167 lakh.
Defence order flow is slow and depends on PSU tendering; management expects 4-6 quarters before a substantial position.
Supply-chain disruption and inflation from the ongoing war; management gave no quantified impact.
Customer concentration: the Jaipur plant depends on one customer under an exclusive arrangement; EV exposure is only about 5.3% of revenue.
Margin target of 18-20% is aspirational and is pushed to FY28, against 13.3% in FY26.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on long-term growth, Vision 2030 and diversification. Candid that Q4 margins and defence ramp-up are still in investment phase, and gave no quantified FY27 revenue guidance beyond the Jaipur figure and a generic double-digit growth view.
key_quotes: FY26 has been a transformational year for Kranti Industries and a significant milestone in our Vision 2030 journey.
We expect double digit growth year on year from here because that is going to happen unless and until something extraordinary does not happen.
However, my experience in this segment is a bit slow so to penetrate and to have a substantial hold on that, it will take another 4-6 quarters at least.
